title: ringswim: ring-walled phase cells from noise swim as crescents and divide, then coarsen into domain-wrapping swimming bands
summary: phase_membrane (chi link ring, noise IC) plus phase_swimdiv's per-body phoretic drift (mu=1.5, now with a MUSCL face flux), or a label-free Gaussian-kernel-averaged drive. With the label drive, bounded walled cells (L rim/core 1.33 aggregate, 31/52 individually membrane-like at seed 0) swim as crescents and divide for ~10000 t, but in every variant tried (label mu 1.5/2/3, kernel sig 6/12/20, mu 1-3, 128^2) swimmers that never starve grow laterally and fuse into one band that wraps the periodic domain (seed 1 by t~13000; kernel sig 20 mu 2 by t~6500). Raising wall tension (Dp 0.25) kills all cells; kernel sig 20 mu 1 stays bounded and divides (gen 5) but barely moves (max 1.9 BL). The missing ingredient is a size limit that works for well-fed swimmers.
